'''Karl Mikhailovich Peterson''' ({{langx|ru|Карл Михайлович Петерсон}}; 25 May 1828 – 1 May 1881) was a Russian [[mathematician]], known by an earlier formulation of the [[Gauss–Codazzi equations]].

== Life and work ==
Peterson was born in a peasant family. He studied at the ''Gymnasium'' of [[Riga]] and, after, at the [[Imperial University of Dorpat]] (now [[Tartu]]) under [[Ferdinand Minding]].<ref>{{smallcaps|Phillips}}, pages 141–2.</ref>

Nothing of his life is known about the ten years after his graduation. In unknown date he went to [[Moscow]] where he taught in the German ''Gymnasium Peter and Paul'' of this city from 1865.<ref>{{smallcaps|Phillips}}, page 157.</ref> Peterson never had an academic position at university level, but he was one of the founders of the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]] with [[Nikolai Brashman]] and [[August Davidov]]. Peterson was a notable collaborator in the journal of the Society and he is considered the founder of the Moscow school of geometry.<ref>{{smallcaps|Laptev & Rozenfeld}}, page 24.</ref>

Peterson gave, in his graduation dissertation (1853, but not published until later), an earliest formulation of the fundamental equations of the surface theory,<ref>{{smallcaps|Reich}}, page 335.</ref> now usually known as [[Gauss–Codazzi equations]], sometimes Peterson–Codazzi equations.

During his time in Moscow, Peterson published some important papers about [[differential geometry]].<ref>{{smallcaps|Phillips}}, pages 156–9.</ref> In 1879, the [[university of Odessa]] awarded him an [[honorary degree]].
